title: Content Systems: how Justin Welsh runs a one-person content engine from newsletter hub to social spokes
summary: Justin explains how he built a solo content system: start with a 30-minute daily habit, add structure each time friction appears, and write one newsletter that gets chopped into many social posts. He also covers niching down and low-friction pricing that follows discovery then trust.

principles.text: Start your content system as a daily 30-minute block, then add tools each time friction appears.
principles.quote: system creation is an iterative process it starts very simply and every time that you hit that block and new friction appears you introduce something new to remove that friction

principles.text: Make a newsletter the pillar piece, then chop it into 5-7 social posts that link back to it.
principles.quote: I ideate I think of an idea and I write a newsletter about it once I've written the newsletter I chop my newsletter into five to seven pieces of content

principles.text: Ideate on a schedule and keep a growing bank of ideas so you never face a blank page.
principles.quote: my goal is to create anywhere from six to ten UniQue Ideas each week when I only need one so I constantly have a growing Repository

principles.text: Use a repeatable copywriting template for every newsletter so writing stays easy.
principles.quote: my newsletter every single week gets pushed through the same template I introduce a problem I introduce why it's important I introduce how most people try and solve the problem

principles.text: Niche down so you're the only one, and offer a non-obvious solution to an obvious problem.
principles.quote: start by saying how can I Niche down so that I'm close to the only or one of five or one of ten people and then how do I bring in non-obvious solution to the table

principles.text: Move people from discovery to trust, then price products as low-friction impulse buys.
principles.quote: I move them from Discovery to trust and then at the end I use pricing that makes it an Impulse Buy
